identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza's fictionalised Formula car for the 2022 to 2025 ground-effect regulations. It shipped as Formula Ultimate Gen2 and was officially rebranded to the Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen3 family in AMS2 v1.6.9, at which point the older 2017 to 2021 hybrid cars became Gen2. No real-world chassis identity is assigned.

notes: Current guided AMS2 testing established move-off, running-shift technique, and cockpit controls with simulator assists disabled.
The modeled car moves from rest without physical clutch input.

This car represents the 2022 to 2025 ground-effect Formula One regulations. Reiza originally shipped it as Formula Ultimate Gen2 and later rebranded it to Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen3, reclassifying the older 2017 to 2021 hybrid cars as Gen2. The pre-rename name is recorded as a retired identity rather than carried here, because the certified build no longer reports it.

The steering lock came from the AMS2 spreadsheet, which records what the simulator applies rather than what the real car was built with. It moves to the simulator layer, where that evidence belongs; no reviewed source establishes the real car's lock.

This record came from the original AMS2 spreadsheet import, where one claim covered the identity, the whole of authentic_controls and the simulator behaviour together. The car has since been driven, and the guided observation establishes those controls directly. The spreadsheet claim no longer reaches authentic_controls, because it describes what the simulator models and cannot settle what the real car had.

driver_summary: Paddle sequential that asks for no clutch at any point: it gets away from rest, cuts the upshift and blips the downshift itself. Once you are in the car the gearbox is not your problem.
